description: Stage 1 of the jabberwock's own curriculum (docs/jabberwock_game_play_design.md): 'I exist; what I control.' Builds on Stage 0's predictor. Control is discovered as in the design: the region the agent CONTROLS is the one whose behaviour is predictable from its action when it is not predictable without it — natively, respond_votes. The new learning is the action_delta MAP: for the controlled region, each action affordance learns the displacement it causes (its dcy/dcx), as an EMA toward the observed motion, written in-fixpoint and FOLDED at the clock edge (the closed loop — the same mechanism as everything). Once learned, the action-conditioned prediction (cy + action_delta[action]) beats the passive constant-velocity prediction whenever the agent changes action. Success (the agent's own): action-conditioned one-step error < passive error for the controlled region.

microtheory.name: stage1_control
microtheory.description: control = the region that responds to me; learn action_delta (each action's displacement) by folding the residual; action-conditioned prediction then beats passive.

rules.name: learn_action_delta
rules.comment: For the controlled region (respond_votes>=2) and the action affordance that was just taken (act.name == game.last_action), learn that action's displacement: EMA its dcy/dcx toward the controlled region's observed motion (drow/dcol). Written as next_dcy/next_dcx (combinational) + clocked=1, so the engine's clock-edge fold commits next_*->* — the closed loop learning the map. dcy/dcx default 0 (Plus[Attr,0]). This is control + the action_delta map under the ONE fold mechanism, no per-event handler.
